cards.q: Return the largest index `i` with `a[i] <= x` in a sorted array, or -1 if there is none.
cards.a: `mid` rounds down, so once `hi == lo + 1` the branch `lo = mid` makes no progress. `a = {1, 2}, x = 2` loops forever. Round up whenever a branch assigns `lo = mid`.

cards.q: Return the first index whose value is at least `x`, or `a.size()` if there is none.
cards.a: With a half-open range the loop must stop at `lo == hi`, but `<=` keeps going and `hi = mid` then changes nothing. `a = {1, 3}, x = 2` loops forever. Use `lo < hi`, which also stops `a[mid]` reading past the end.

cards.q: Find the minimum of a non-empty rotated sorted array with distinct values.
cards.a: When `a[mid] <= a[hi]`, `mid` itself can be the minimum, and `hi = mid - 1` throws it away. `a = {3, 1, 2}` returns 3 instead of 1. Keep it with `hi = mid`.

cards.q: Return the index of `x` in a rotated sorted array with distinct values, or -1.
cards.a: When `lo == mid` the left part is the single element `a[lo]`, but strict `<` sends the code to the branch for a sorted right part. `a = {3, 1}, x = 1` returns -1 instead of 1. Test `a[lo] <= a[mid]`.

cards.q: Return the integer square root of a non-negative int `n`: the largest `r` with `r * r <= n`.
cards.a: `mid * mid` is computed in `int` and overflows once `mid` passes 46340. `n = 2147483647` overflows on the first probe, and a plain build wraps to 0 and returns 1073741824 instead of 46340. Compare in 64 bits with `(long long)mid * mid <= n`.
cards.code: if ((long long)mid * mid <= n) lo = mid;

cards.q: Versions `1..n` turn bad at some point and stay bad. Return the first bad version for any int `n`.
cards.a: `lo + hi` overflows `int` when the sum passes `INT_MAX`. `n = 2147483647` overflows on the first step, and the negative `mid` keeps the loop from ever reaching the answer. Write `mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2`.

cards.q: Find the smallest ship capacity that moves a non-empty package list, in order, within `days` days.
cards.a: Capacity must start at the heaviest package, because the feasibility check still loads a package that exceeds `cap`. `w = {5, 5}, days = 3` returns 1 instead of 5. Start `lo` at `*max_element(w.begin(), w.end())`.
cards.code: long long lo = *max_element(w.begin(), w.end()), hi = accumulate(w.begin(), w.end(), 0LL);

cards.q: Return the length of the longest substring with no repeated character.
cards.a: `last` still holds characters that already left the window, so `lo` can jump backwards. `s = "abba"` returns 3 instead of 2. Only move forward with `lo = max(lo, last[s[hi]] + 1)`.

cards.q: Given positive integers and `target > 0`, return the shortest subarray length with sum at least `target`, or 0.
cards.a: The length is recorded after the shrink, so it describes a window that may no longer meet the target. `a = {5}, target = 5` returns 0 instead of 1. Update `best` first, then remove `a[lo]`.
cards.code:
best = min(best, hi - lo + 1);
sum -= a[lo++];

cards.q: Return the length of the longest substring with at most `k` distinct characters.
cards.a: A key whose count reaches 0 stays in the map, so `cnt.size()` never drops. `s = "abac", k = 2` keeps shrinking and runs `lo` off the end of the string. Erase the key when its count hits 0.

cards.q: Return the length of the shortest window of `s` containing every character of `t` with multiplicity, or 0.
cards.a: After the decrement a required character is short only when `have < need`, so `<=` also fires for spare characters and ends the shrink early. `s = "xa", t = "a"` returns 2 instead of 1. Use strict `<`.

cards.q: Return the maximum of every window of size `k`, with `1 <= k <= a.size()`.
cards.a: The window ending at `i` starts at `i - k + 1`, so index `i - k` is already out, yet `<` keeps it for one extra step. `a = {3, 1, 1}, k = 2` returns `{3, 3}` instead of `{3, 1}`. Pop when `dq.front() <= i - k`.

cards.q: Return all unique triplets of values that sum to zero.
cards.a: Comparing with `a[i + 1]` skips the first copy of a value, so triplets that use that value twice are lost. `a = {-1, -1, 2}` returns nothing instead of `{-1, -1, 2}`. Skip only repeats of the previous anchor: `if (i > 0 && a[i] == a[i - 1]) continue;`.

cards.q: In a sorted array, keep each value at most twice in place and return the new length.
cards.a: `a[i - 2]` may already have been overwritten by the write pointer, so the check reads shifted data. `a = {1, 1, 1, 2, 2}` returns 3 instead of 4. Compare with what was kept: `if (w < 2 || a[i] != a[w - 2])`.

cards.q: Return every distinct subset of a list that may contain repeated values.
cards.a: Duplicates should only be skipped among siblings at one depth, but `i > 0` also blocks taking a second copy deeper down. `a = {1, 1}` returns `{}, {1}` and misses `{1, 1}`. Use `if (i > start && a[i] == a[i - 1]) continue;`.

cards.q: Count the subarrays whose sum equals `k`; values may be negative.
cards.a: The empty prefix is missing, so subarrays that start at index 0 are never counted. `a = {3}, k = 3` returns 0 instead of 1. Seed the map with sum 0 seen once.

cards.q: Return the length of the longest subarray whose sum equals `k`; values may be negative.
cards.a: A repeated prefix sum overwrites its earliest index, and the longest subarray needs the earliest one. `a = {1, -1, 1}, k = 1` returns 1 instead of 3. Store only the first occurrence with `first.emplace(pre, i);`.

cards.q: Count the subarrays of an integer array whose sum is divisible by `k > 0`.
cards.a: In C++ `%` keeps the sign of the left operand, so prefix -1 lands on index -1 instead of matching prefix 2. `a = {2, -3}, k = 3` reads `seen[-1]` and misses the subarray `{-3}`. Normalize with `pre = ((pre + x) % k + k) % k;`.

cards.q: For each element, return the next greater value to its right, or -1.
cards.a: `<=` pops on an equal value and records it as the answer. `a = {2, 2, 3}` returns `{2, 3, -1}` instead of `{3, 3, -1}`. Pop only on strict `<`.

cards.q: Return the sum of the minimum of every contiguous subarray.
cards.a: Both passes stop at an equal value, so a subarray with a tied minimum belongs to no index. `a = {1, 1}` returns 2 instead of 3. Make the left pass pop on `>=` so each tie has exactly one owner.

cards.q: Return the largest rectangle area in a histogram.
cards.a: Bars still on the stack when the loop ends are never measured. `h = {1, 2, 3}` returns 0 instead of 4. Append a 0 bar before the loop so every bar gets popped.

cards.q: Compute how much rain water is trapped between the bars.
cards.a: After popping `bottom` the stack may be empty, so `st.back()` is undefined. `h = {1, 2}` reads an empty stack. Add `if (st.empty()) break;` right after the pop, since no left wall means no water.

cards.q: Remove the `n`-th node from the end of a list, with `1 <= n <= length`.
cards.a: When `n` equals the length the head is the target, `fast` ends up null and `fast->next` crashes. List `[1, 2]` with `n = 2` dereferences null. Return `head->next` when `fast` is null, or start both pointers from a dummy node.

cards.q: Return the middle node of a list; for even length return the second middle.
cards.a: On an even-length list `fast` jumps to null, and the next loop test dereferences it. List `[1, 2]` crashes on the second check. Test both: `while (fast && fast->next)`.

cards.q: Return whether a singly linked list contains a cycle.
cards.a: Both pointers start equal, so the loop body never runs and the result only says the list has two nodes. List `[1, 2]` with no cycle returns true. Start `fast` one step ahead, at `head->next` when `head` is not null.

cards.q: Merge two sorted lists by relinking their nodes.
cards.a: Only the rest of `a` is attached, so whatever remains of `b` is dropped. `a = []`, `b = [1]` returns an empty list. Attach whichever of `a` and `b` is still non-null.

cards.q: Delete every node whose value equals `x`.
cards.a: The scan only inspects `cur->next`, so the head itself is never checked. List `[1, 2]` with `x = 1` stays `[1, 2]`. Start `cur` at a dummy node placed before the head and return `dummy.next`.

cards.q: Return the node where two lists meet, or null if they never meet.
cards.a: The pointers switch lists without ever stepping onto null, so disjoint lists never become equal. `a = [1]`, `b = [2]` loops forever. Let each pointer step onto null once before it switches lists.
cards.code:
p = p ? p->next : b;
q = q ? q->next : a;

cards.q: Implement an LRU cache with capacity `cap >= 1` and non-negative values. `get` returns -1 for a missing key.
cards.a: After `pop_back`, `items.back()` is a different entry, so the wrong key is erased and the evicted key keeps a dead iterator. With `cap = 2`, `put(1, 1), put(2, 2), put(3, 3), get(2)` returns -1 instead of 2. Erase from `pos` before `pop_back`.

cards.q: Return the number of nodes on the shortest path from the root down to a leaf.
cards.a: A missing child returns depth 0, so `min` picks a path that ends at a node with one child, which is not a leaf. Root 1 with only left child 2 returns 1 instead of 2. When one child is null, recurse only into the other.
cards.code:
if (!root->left) return 1 + minDepth(root->right);
if (!root->right) return 1 + minDepth(root->left);

cards.q: Return whether some root-to-leaf path sums to `target`.
cards.a: Stopping at null accepts a path that ends at an inner node with one child. Root 1 with only left child 2 and `target = 1` returns true instead of false. Return false at null and compare the target at a real leaf.
cards.code:
if (!root) return false;
if (!root->left && !root->right) return target == root->val;

cards.q: Return the diameter of a binary tree in edges. The function is called once per tree on many trees.
cards.a: `best` is global and keeps the value from the previous tree. A 3-node chain followed by a single node returns 2 for the second tree instead of 0. Reset with `best = 0;` before calling `height`.

cards.q: Return the values of a binary tree grouped by level, top to bottom.
cards.a: `q.size()` is read again on every pass while children are being pushed, so the level boundary moves. Root 1 with children 2 and 3 returns `{{1, 2}, {3}}` instead of `{{1}, {2, 3}}`. Freeze the size before the loop.
cards.code: for (int i = 0, sz = q.size(); i < sz; i++)

cards.q: Return whether a binary tree is a valid BST with distinct values in `[-2^31, 2^31 - 1]`.
cards.a: `n->val + 1` overflows at `INT_MAX`, so the lower bound of the right subtree wraps to `INT_MIN`. Root `INT_MAX` with right child 5 returns true instead of false. Use `long long` bounds and add `1LL`, because `n->val + 1` alone is still computed in `int`.
cards.code:
bool check(TreeNode* n, long long lo, long long hi)
return check(n->left, lo, n->val - 1LL) && check(n->right, n->val + 1LL, hi);

cards.q: Return whether a binary tree is a valid BST with values in `[-2^31, 2^31 - 1]`.
cards.a: The open bounds cannot express no limit in `int`, so a legal node equal to `INT_MAX` or `INT_MIN` is rejected. A single node 2147483647 returns false instead of true. Make the bounds `long long` and start from `LLONG_MIN` and `LLONG_MAX`.
cards.code:
bool check(TreeNode* n, long long lo, long long hi)
return check(root, LLONG_MIN, LLONG_MAX);

cards.q: Insert `x` into a BST through its root pointer.
cards.a: `root` is a copy of the caller's pointer, so the new node is assigned to a local and lost. Inserting 5 into an empty tree leaves the caller's root null. Take the pointer by reference: `TreeNode*& root`.

cards.q: Return the `k`-th smallest value in a BST, with `k` counted from 1.
cards.a: `k` is passed by value, so a visit in the left subtree does not reduce the caller's count. Root 2 with children 1 and 3 and `k = 1` returns 2 instead of 1. Share one counter with `int& k`.
cards.code: void walk(TreeNode* n, int& k, int& ans)

cards.q: Return the sum of all left leaves in a binary tree.
cards.a: `n->left` is dereferenced before anyone checks that it exists. A single node crashes. Guard with `n->left && ...`, and the `else` then handles the null child through the base case.

cards.q: Return the BFS edge distance from `s` to every node, or -1 if a node is unreachable.
cards.a: Nodes are marked when popped, so a node already in the queue can be pushed again and get a larger distance. `g = {{1, 2}, {2}, {}}, s = 0` gives `dist[2] = 2` instead of 1. Mark at push: set `seen[s]` before the loop and `seen[v]` inside the `if`, and drop `seen[u] = 1`.

cards.q: Return the shortest distances from `s` in a graph with non-negative edge weights.
cards.a: `done[v]` is set on the first relaxation, which freezes a tentative distance before a cheaper path can improve it. Edges `0->1` weight 10, `0->2` weight 1, `2->1` weight 1 give `dist[1] = 10` instead of 2. Finalize at pop: `if (done[u]) continue; done[u] = 1;`, and remove the line in the relax.

cards.q: Count the nodes whose shortest distance from `s` is at most `limit`; weights are non-negative.
cards.a: A node improved twice has two heap entries, and the stale one is counted as well. Edges `0->1` weight 5, `0->2` weight 1, `2->1` weight 1 with `limit = 10` return 4 instead of 3. Skip stale entries right after the pop with `if (d > dist[u]) continue;`.

cards.q: Return whether a directed graph contains a cycle.
cards.a: A node stays marked after its DFS finishes, so reaching it again by a second path looks like a back edge. The diamond `g = {{1, 2}, {3}, {3}, {}}` returns true instead of false. Use three states and set `state[u] = 2` when the node finishes; only state 1 means a cycle.

cards.q: Deep-copy a connected undirected graph, starting from one node.
cards.a: The clone is recorded only after its neighbours are visited, so a neighbour that points back recurses again. Two nodes linked to each other overflow the stack. Set `seen[n] = copy` before the loop.
cards.code:
seen[n] = copy;
for (Node* m : n->nbrs) copy->nbrs.push_back(cloneGraph(m, seen));

cards.q: Compute single-source shortest paths with a binary heap; weights are non-negative.
cards.a: `d` and `u` are bound to the heap's top slot, which `pop` and later pushes overwrite or free. Edges `0->1` weight 1 and `0->2` weight 5 gave `dist[2] = 6` instead of 5 in a plain build, because the first push changed `d`. Copy the entry: `auto [d, u] = pq.top();`.

cards.q: Return a topological order of `n` nodes, or an empty vector if none exists.
cards.a: Nodes on a cycle never reach indegree 0, so the loop just stops and returns a partial order. `n = 3` with edges `1->2`, `2->1` returns `{0}` instead of `{}`. Return the order only if its size equals `n`.

cards.q: Return whether `n` tasks can all finish given dependency edges `u -> v`.
cards.a: The `set` drops a repeated edge but `indeg` still counts it, so `v` never reaches 0. `n = 2` with the edge `0->1` listed twice returns false instead of true. Count only new edges: `if (g[u].insert(v).second) indeg[v]++;`.

cards.q: Implement union-find, where `connected` reports whether two elements share a set.
cards.a: `unite` re-parents element `a` instead of its root, which cuts `a` away from its old set. `unite(0, 1)` then `unite(0, 2)` leaves `connected(1, 2)` false. Link the roots: `p[find(a)] = find(b);`.
cards.code: void unite(int a, int b) { p[find(a)] = find(b); }

cards.q: Count the connected components of `n` nodes given undirected edges.
cards.a: `p[i]` is only a parent, not necessarily the root, because compression happens only on nodes that `find` visited. `n = 4` with edges `(0, 1), (2, 3), (0, 2)` returns 2 instead of 1. Insert `find(i)` for every `i` instead.
cards.code:
set<int> roots;
for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) roots.insert(find(i));

cards.q: Implement union-find that stays fast on `2 * 10^5` elements and as many queries.
cards.a: Parents are never shortened and unions are not balanced, so a chain costs O(n) per `find`. Uniting `(i, i + 1)` for `n = 200000` and then calling `find(0)` `n` times does about 4 * 10^10 steps and times out. Halve the path while walking: `x = p[x] = p[p[x]]`.

cards.q: Return the cheapest price from `s` to `t` using at most `k + 1` flights, or -1.
cards.a: Relaxing in place lets one round chain several flights, so a round can use more than one hop. Flights `0->1` price 1, `1->2` price 1, `0->2` price 5 with `k = 0` return 2 instead of 5. Copy `dist` at the start of each round and read `prev[u]`.
cards.code:
vector<int> prev = dist;
if (prev[u] != INF && prev[u] + w < dist[v]) dist[v] = prev[u] + w;

cards.q: Return whether word `w` can be traced through adjacent grid cells without reusing a cell.
cards.a: The `#` mark is never undone, so a failed attempt keeps blocking cells that a later start needs. `g = {"aa", "bz"}, w = "aab"` returns false instead of true. Save the result of the recursive calls, restore `g[r][c] = w[i]`, then return.

cards.q: Count the ways to place `n` non-attacking queens on an `n` by `n` board.
cards.a: `r - c` is negative whenever `c > r`, so `d2` is indexed out of bounds. `n = 4` reads `d2[-1]` on the second column of the first row. Shift the index to `r - c + n`.

cards.q: Solve 0/1 knapsack with a rolling previous row.
cards.a: `prev` is a reference, so it is the same row as `cur` and an item can be taken twice. `w = {1}, v = {10}, cap = 2` returns 20 instead of 10. Take a real copy: `vector<int> prev = cur;`.

cards.q: Solve 0/1 knapsack with a one-dimensional table.
cards.a: Going upward reads `dp[c - w[i]]` after this same item already updated it, which is the unbounded version. `w = {1}, v = {10}, cap = 2` returns 20 instead of 10. Iterate capacity downward.
cards.code: for (int c = cap; c >= w[i]; c--)

cards.q: Count the combinations of distinct coin values that sum to `amount`, where each coin may repeat and order does not matter.
cards.a: With amounts on the outside, each order of the same coins is counted separately. `coins = {1, 2}, amount = 3` returns 3 instead of 2. Loop over coins on the outside and amounts on the inside.

cards.q: Return the fewest coins that sum to `amount`, or -1 if it cannot be done.
cards.a: `dp[a - c]` can still be `INT_MAX`, and adding 1 overflows to a negative count that `min` keeps. `coins = {2}, amount = 3` returns a negative number instead of -1. Skip unreachable states with `dp[a - c] != INT_MAX`.
cards.code: if (c <= a && dp[a - c] != INT_MAX) dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a - c] + 1);

cards.q: Return the edit distance between two strings using insert, delete and replace.
cards.a: Only the first column is initialized, so turning an empty prefix into `b[0..j)` costs 0. `a = "", b = "ab"` returns 0 instead of 2. Add `for (int j = 1; j <= n; j++) dp[0][j] = j;`.
cards.code: for (int j = 1; j <= n; j++) dp[0][j] = j;

cards.q: Count the palindromic substrings of `s` with an interval table.
cards.a: `dp[i][j]` depends on `dp[i + 1][j - 1]`, which a top-down `i` has not filled yet and reads as 0. `s = "aba"` returns 3 instead of 4. Run `i` from `n - 1` down to 0.

cards.q: Sink an island of `1` cells to `0` from a starting cell.
cards.a: The cell is read before the bounds are checked, and `||` evaluates left to right. `g = {"1"}` from `(0, 0)` reads `g[1]` on the first recursive call. Put all four bounds tests before `g[r][c]`.
cards.code:
if (r < 0 || c < 0 || r >= (int)g.size() || c >= (int)g[0].size() ||
    g[r][c] != '1') return;

cards.q: Return the `k`-th smallest element using a heap of at most `k` items, with `1 <= k <= a.size()`.
cards.a: A min-heap pops the smallest, so it keeps the `k` largest and returns the `k`-th largest. `a = {1, 2, 3}, k = 1` returns 3 instead of 1. Use a max-heap: `priority_queue<int> pq;`.

cards.q: Merge `k` sorted lists with a heap of list heads.
cards.a: `priority_queue` pops the element that compares greatest, so `<` yields the largest head first. Lists `[1, 2]` and `[3]` return `[3, 1, 2]` instead of `[1, 2, 3]`. Flip it to `a->val > b->val` for a min-heap.

cards.q: Sort players by score, highest first.
cards.a: `sort` requires a strict weak ordering, and `>=` claims two equal items each come first. 100 players with the same score is undefined behaviour and can read past the end of the array. Use strict `a.score > b.score`.

cards.q: Return the fewest rooms needed for half-open meetings `[start, end)`.
cards.a: The comparator ignores `d`, so at equal times a start can run before an end. `{{2, 3}, {1, 2}}` returns 2 instead of 1. Use plain `sort(ev.begin(), ev.end());`, which puts -1 before +1 at the same time.

cards.q: Remove all even values from `a` in place.
cards.a: `erase` invalidates `it` and shifts the next element into its slot, which `++it` then skips. `a = {2, 4}` leaves `{4}` instead of `{}`. Use `it = a.erase(it)` and advance only when nothing was erased.

cards.q: Return `start >= 1` followed by its repeated halvings, ending at 1.
cards.a: `push_back` inside a range-for invalidates its hidden iterators, and `end()` was fixed before the loop started. `start = 8` returns `{8, 4}` instead of `{8, 4, 2, 1}`. Loop by index and re-read `out.size()`.

cards.q: Sort the values and drop duplicates.
cards.a: `erase` with one iterator removes a single element, not the tail, and `unique` may return `end()`. `a = {1, 1, 1}` returns `{1, 1}` instead of `{1}`. Erase the range: `a.erase(last, a.end());`.

cards.q: Return whether any two adjacent elements are equal.
cards.a: `a.size()` is unsigned, so `a.size() - 1` wraps to a huge value on an empty vector. `a = {}` reads out of bounds instead of returning false. Move the arithmetic to the safe side: `i + 1 < a.size()`.

cards.q: Return the leftmost index where the sum to its left equals the sum to its right, or -1.
cards.a: `accumulate` takes its working type from the initial value, so `0` sums in `int` even though `total` is `long long`. `a = {2000000000, 2000000000, 2000000000}` overflows and returns -1 instead of 1. Pass `0LL`.

cards.q: Return whether `s` can be split into words from `dict`.
cards.a: The second argument of `substr` is a length, not an end index, so the piece is too long. `s = "abc"` with `dict = {"a", "b", "c"}` returns false instead of true. Write `s.substr(j, i - j)`.
cards.code: if (dp[j] && dict.count(s.substr(j, i - j))) { dp[i] = 1; break; }

cards.q: Return the longest palindromic substring of `s`.
cards.a: When the loop stops, `l` and `r` sit one step outside the palindrome, so its length is `r - l - 1` and it starts at `l + 1`. `s = "a"` gets `start = -1`, and `substr` throws `out_of_range`. Record `bestLen = r - l - 1` and `start = l + 1`.
cards.code: if (r - l - 1 > bestLen) { bestLen = r - l - 1; start = l + 1; }

cards.q: Return indices `{i, j}` with `i < j` and `a[i] + a[j] == target`, or `{}` if there are none.
cards.a: `pos[key]` inserts a default 0 on a miss, and a real partner at index 0 also reads as false. `a = {3, 4}, target = 7` returns `{}` instead of `{0, 1}`. Look up with `find` so a stored 0 and a missing key stay different.
cards.code:
auto it = pos.find(target - a[i]);
if (it != pos.end()) return {it->second, i};

cards.q: Support prefix queries and a word count on a map-based trie.
cards.a: `t->kids[c]` inserts a null child on every failed lookup, and `countWords` later follows it. With only `"a"` stored, `hasPrefix(root, "b")` then `countWords(root)` crashes. Use `find` in `hasPrefix` so a query never changes the trie.

cards.q: Sum the integers on each line of text and return one total per line.
cards.a: Reading to the end sets the stream's fail and eof flags, and `str()` does not clear them. `lines = {"1 2", "3"}` returns `{3, 0}` instead of `{3, 3}`. Call `ss.clear();` for every line.

cards.q: Return the largest sum of non-adjacent elements from a list of non-negative values.
cards.a: The base case touches index 1, which does not exist for a single element. `a = {7}` reads `a[1]` and writes `dp[1]`. Add `if (n == 1) return a[0];`.

cards.q: Return whether two strings are at most one insert, delete or replace apart.
cards.a: `size()` is unsigned, so when `a` is shorter the difference wraps to a huge value instead of going negative. `a = "a", b = "ab"` returns false instead of true. Subtract the smaller size from the larger one.
cards.code: if (max(a.size(), b.size()) - min(a.size(), b.size()) > 1) return false;
